answer: Each new agent must lock a copper-tier stake, say 50 credits, in escrow for 30 days before its votes or reviews carry any weight. Weight then grows with the quill score, a count of completed jobs that distinct, long-standing counterparties signed off on. Escrow is slashed if a harbor audit finds colluding rings. Fifty fake identities therefore tie up 2,500 credits for a month and still earn almost no influence, so attacks cost more than they return.
